concept_name: Bohr Model — Discrete Energy Levels and the Line Spectrum
section: Unit 2 — Structure of Atom (Bohr's model, energy levels, line spectrum)
source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Unit 2 'Structure of Atom' — chapter-index scope reference only; teaching, examples, and phrasing authored from first principles. NCERT Exemplar consulted for misconception beliefs only. First chemistry concept through the pipeline (Wave 1, prove-first).

real_world_anchor.primary: A gas-discharge sign glowing one specific colour. Shine a hot filament's white light through a prism and you get a full rainbow. Shine the glowing gas's light through the same prism and you get only a few razor-sharp coloured lines, with darkness between them. Same prism, utterly different answer — and that mystery is exactly this concept; its resolution, the atom's fixed energy staircase, is the payoff.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Astronomers read a star's composition purely from the lines in its light, without ever visiting it — the same fingerprint principle, read across light-years instead of a lab bench.

hc_eV_nm.name: h·c convenience constant
hc_eV_nm.role: TEACHING-ROUNDED (precise 1239.84); reproduces every displayed λ to whole-nm

E_ionisation_ev.name: H ionisation energy (n=1→∞)
E_ionisation_ev.role: STATE_8 only; n=∞ outside slider domain by design

lambda_nm.formula: hc_eV_nm / delta_E_ev, whole-nm, GUARDED null when n_start==n_end

direction.formula: 'absorb'|'emit'|'none' — drives photon arrow direction + in/out ledger word

spectral_region.formula: 'UV'|'VISIBLE'|'IR' — gates whether a mark is painted on the 400–700 nm strip

constraints: energy conservation: ΔE_photon = E_high − E_low EXACTLY for every displayed transition; energy in = energy out
E_n = −13.6/n² eV for hydrogen (Z=1); n is a positive integer ≥ 1, never fractional or zero
absorption (n_end > n_start) needs an incoming photon of EXACTLY ΔE; any other energy passes through unabsorbed
emission (n_end < n_start) releases exactly ONE photon of energy ΔE — never more, never less
n_start = n_end ⇒ ΔE = 0 ⇒ no photon, no line — MUST be guarded (λ division-by-zero), never NaN/Infinity on canvas
λ = hc/ΔE uses hc = 1240 eV·nm (rounded teaching constant) — rounding is for whole-nm display only, never propagated into stored ΔE

STATE_1.title: Rainbow vs Four Lines — The Mystery

tts_sentences.text_en: A hot filament's white light splits into a full rainbow.
A glowing gas tube's light splits into just four sharp coloured lines, with darkness between them.
Same prism. Utterly different answer.
Why does a glowing gas make only a few sharp colours?
Zoom inside one hydrogen atom.
Its electron's energy comes in fixed rungs, an energy level or shell, n equals one, two, three and up, each rung less negative than the one below.
Negative just means bound; n equals one is the floor, so the atom never collapses.
The four mystery lines wait below, ghosted.
If energy could be any value, an electron could glide and rest anywhere between rungs — watch the ghost try.
It can't. That smooth path is impossible, and the smear fades.
The real electron only snaps rung to rung, never pausing between.
Energy in an atom is a staircase, not a ramp.

misconception_watch.belief: electron energy is continuous — it can sit at any energy
misconception_watch.visual_counter: ghost rests mid-gap + continuous smear, then dissolves as the real electron snaps rung-to-rung
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: energy in an atom is a staircase, not a ramp.

scene_composition.text: electron held by the nucleus — light arrives in fixed photon packets

tts_sentences.text_en: An eleven electron-volt photon arrives, passes straight through — nothing matches, so nothing happens.
Now a twelve-point-oh-nine electron-volt photon arrives, exactly the one-to-three gap.
It is swallowed whole, and the electron jumps from level one to level three.
Photon in: twelve-point-oh-nine electron-volts. Gap: twelve-point-oh-nine electron-volts. An exact match.
The electron, still up on level three, drops back to level two.
A beat later a one-point-eight-nine electron-volt photon flies out, and it paints the red six-fifty-six nanometre line solid.
Up swallows a photon; down spits one out.

misconception_watch.belief: absorption and emission are the same process/direction
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the photon arrow's flight direction reverses (in→out) while the jump direction flips with it — the STATE_4/STATE_5 pair
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: up swallows a photon, down spits one out.

STATE_6.title: Every Line Is a Gap — The Fingerprint

scene_composition.text: one atom shown — a real lamp: ~10²² atoms/s

tts_sentences.text_en: Three more drops follow: four to two, five to two, six to two — painting ghosted lines solid at four-eighty-six, four-thirty-four, four-ten nanometres.
Every line is one exact energy gap made visible — the atom's fingerprint.
One atom here; a real lamp holds ten-to-the-twenty-two, jumping every second.
Stars read their recipe the same way.

STATE_7.title: Lock the Numbers — ΔE = hν = hc/λ

tts_sentences.text_en: Lock the numbers: energy gap delta E equals h nu equals h c over lambda.
Replayed slow: minus one-point-five-one minus minus three-point-four gives one-point-eight-nine electron-volts.
Wavelength lambda equals twelve-forty over one-point-eight-nine — six-fifty-six nanometres.
Pick the bigger four-to-two gap and lambda shrinks: bigger gap, shorter wavelength.

misconception_watch.belief: a bigger jump gives a longer wavelength
misconception_watch.visual_counter: selector shows the BIGGEST gap (4→2) at the SHORT-λ end, λ = hc/ΔE computed live
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: λ = hc/ΔE — bigger gap, shorter wavelength.

tts_sentences.text_en: One formula predicts every rung: energy level E sub n equals minus thirteen-point-six over n squared electron-volts.
Levels seven, eight, nine crowd upward toward a dashed line at E equals zero — fully free.
Give the level-one electron exactly thirteen-point-six electron-volts and it ejects clean off the ladder — ionised, free at last.

scene_composition.text: {direction==='none' ? 'Pick two different levels' : ((direction==='absorb' ? 'Photon absorbed' : 'Photon emitted') + ' — gap ' + delta_E_ev.toFixed(2) + ' eV,  λ = ' + (lambda_nm===null?'—':lambda_nm) + ' nm' + (spectral_region==='VISIBLE' ? ' — visible line' : ' — not visible'))}

tts_sentences.text_en: Pick any two levels — watch the jump, the photon, and the line appear.

regeneration_variants.label: Same physics, different lamp (a neon sign instead of a lab discharge tube)
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A neon advertising sign glows a specific colour instead of a lab hydrogen discharge tube; the SAME hydrogen Balmer lines (656/486/434/410 nm) stay the teaching example — the anchor object (the lamp) changes, not the atom.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical Bohr energy-level ladder, identical ΔE = hν = hc/λ lock, identical four-line fingerprint; only the real-world anchor object changes.

aha_moment.statement: Each coloured line in a glowing gas IS one exact atomic energy gap made visible.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who reaches 80–85% understands: energy in an atom is quantised into fixed levels, not continuous; absorption requires an exact energy match while emission releases exactly the gap; every spectral line is one specific energy gap made visible, together explaining why a glowing gas shows a line spectrum, not a rainbow; and can compute ΔE and λ using Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV and hc = 1240 eV·nm, including recognising ionisation as reaching E = 0.

questions.stem: Inside a hydrogen atom, which statement about the electron's energy is correct?

options.A: The electron can have any energy value, including values between two levels.
options.B: The electron can only have certain fixed energy values — never anything in between.
options.C: The electron's energy is always zero unless a photon hits it.
options.D: The electron's energy depends only on the size of the atom, not on n.

distractor_misconceptions.A: the continuous-energy misconception — believing energy can take any value, like a ramp
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses 'ground state' with 'zero energy' — ignores that n=1 already has a large negative (bound) energy
distractor_misconceptions.D: ignores that n directly sets the level's energy via Eₙ = −13.6/n²

questions.parallel_form_stem: A student says an atom's electron could rest exactly halfway between n=2 and n=3 if it had the right energy. Is this possible?

questions.stem: Why does a glowing hydrogen gas emit only a few sharp coloured lines instead of a full rainbow?

options.A: The gas is too thin to produce every colour.
options.B: Each line corresponds to one exact energy gap between two atomic levels — only those gaps exist.
options.C: The prism used for gases is different from the one used for filaments.
options.D: Gas atoms move too fast to show all colours.

distractor_misconceptions.A: misattributes the effect to gas density/thickness rather than discrete energy structure
distractor_misconceptions.C: wrongly blames the measuring instrument instead of the atom's structure
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses thermal motion with the cause of spectral discreteness

questions.tested_idea: line spectrum as the visible fingerprint of discrete energy gaps
questions.parallel_form_stem: A star's light shows dark absorption lines at very specific wavelengths, never a full rainbow gap. What does this tell you about the atoms in its outer layers?

questions.stem: When an electron drops from a higher energy level to a lower one, what happens?

options.A: It absorbs a photon of energy equal to the gap.
options.B: It emits a photon of energy equal to the gap.
options.C: It absorbs and emits a photon at the same time.
options.D: Nothing happens — only upward jumps involve photons.

distractor_misconceptions.A: reverses absorption and emission — believes both processes look the same
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents a simultaneous absorb+emit process that doesn't occur for a single transition
distractor_misconceptions.D: wrongly believes only absorption involves a photon, ignoring emission entirely

questions.tested_idea: absorption vs emission direction (up = in, down = out)
questions.parallel_form_stem: An electron jumps from n=4 to n=2. Does the atom gain or release a photon, and why?

questions.stem: Using Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV and hc = 1240 eV·nm, an electron drops from n=4 (−0.85 eV) to n=2 (−3.40 eV). What is the emitted wavelength?

options.B: ≈ 730 nm — bigger gaps make longer wavelengths
options.C: 1240 nm — using hc directly without dividing by ΔE
options.D: 2.55 nm — dividing ΔE by hc instead of the reverse

distractor_misconceptions.C: forgets to compute ΔE first before dividing hc by it
distractor_misconceptions.D: inverts the formula, computing ΔE/hc instead of hc/ΔE

questions.tested_idea: λ = hc/ΔE arithmetic and the inverse energy-wavelength relation
questions.parallel_form_stem: An electron drops from n=5 to n=2 (ΔE = 2.86 eV). Using hc = 1240 eV·nm, which wavelength is emitted?

questions.stem: A photon carrying 11.00 eV strikes a hydrogen atom whose electron sits at n=1. The 1→2 gap is 10.20 eV and the 1→3 gap is 12.09 eV. What happens?

options.A: The photon passes straight through — its energy matches no gap exactly.
options.B: The electron absorbs part of the photon's energy and jumps partway.
options.C: The electron jumps to n=2, absorbing only 10.20 eV and losing the rest as heat.
options.D: The electron jumps to n=3, since 11.00 eV is close enough to 12.09 eV.

distractor_misconceptions.B: invents partial absorption — energy levels are discrete, an electron cannot absorb PART of a photon
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents a 'leftover energy as heat' escape hatch that violates the exact-match rule
distractor_misconceptions.D: the 'close enough' misconception — ignores that the match must be EXACT

questions.tested_idea: exact energy match required for absorption (no partial or close-enough jumps)
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 9.00 eV photon reaches a level-1 electron whose only gaps are 10.20 eV (to n=2) and 12.09 eV (to n=3). Does the atom absorb it?

questions.stem: How much energy is needed to completely free (ionise) an electron sitting at n=1 in hydrogen (E₁ = −13.60 eV)?

options.A: 13.60 eV — exactly enough to raise the electron's energy from −13.60 eV to 0.
options.B: −13.60 eV, since that is the electron's own energy.
options.C: 6.80 eV, half of the ground-state energy.
options.D: Infinite energy, since n can never reach ∞ in practice.

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses the electron's bound energy with the energy REQUIRED to free it (sign/magnitude confusion)
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents an arbitrary halving rule with no basis in Eₙ = −13.6/n²
distractor_misconceptions.D: wrongly believes ionisation requires literally reaching n=∞ rather than reaching E=0

questions.tested_idea: ionisation energy = raising Eₙ to the E=0 free-electron reference
questions.parallel_form_stem: If a hypothetical level n=1 electron already had E = −6.80 eV instead of −13.60 eV, how much energy would ionise it?
